newsitem.title: ROMANIA: BUCHAREST SHARES MIXED, VOLUME, TURNOVER DOWN.
newsitem.headline: BUCHAREST SHARES MIXED, VOLUME, TURNOVER DOWN.

text.p: Bucharest share prices moved
sideways on Friday, when volumes and turnover fell in what
brokers called quiet trading in a typical end-week session.
"On the buying side we had investors unwilling to pay too
much for stocks they say are already too expensive and on the
selling side supply wasn't that strong," said a trader.
Three independent market indices, the VAB, the BIG and the
CAS-SE, based on average prices and market capitalisation,
moved lower from the previous session, slipping 2.3, 2.29 and
2.27 percent respectively from Thursday.
The average price of 17 stocks pushed ahead -- with more
significant price rises on the second tier. Twenty listings
edged down and five remained flat. Four companies had no deals
and two were suspended.
Volume thinned to 2.3 million shares from 3.9 million on
Thursday and turnover slipped 8.7 billion lei to 10.6 billion.
First-tier stocks traded more heavily, taking 70 percent of
total volume and 78 percent of turnover.
Fertiliser maker Azomures was the most active
listing in this section, trading almost 541,000 shares. It
closed 50 lei lower at 3,750.
On the lower tier, Ciprom steel pipe maker
dominated trading. It closed weaker under selling pressure in
late trading, shedding 200 lei to 1,600.
Newcomer Aeroteh airplane equipment maker traded 200 shares
and closed at 30,000 lei, unchanged from the opening.
